reviews.strengths:
- Small footprint: one block at the head of the pass-3 leftover loop, round 1 only, at most one unit per plan, no scoring change. The plan is built once per movement phase, so in practice that is one unit per player per game. FIX_RANGED_CENTRE 0 skips the block, so the base is restored exactly.
- At all three findings it gives exactly the measured branch (same unit, obj_center, Advance). The ADVANCE branch in execution runs before T7-26, so the Heavy hold cannot undo it.
- By construction it cannot touch keepers, capture-pass orders, SCREEN-earmarked units (they are withheld from candidates), round 2 onward, or a centre trip that is race-hopeless or TOO-LATE. It also needs another unit already committed to the centre.
- It leaves the measured unit's order unchanged at all six guardrails, and at the r5c06 Lootas-capture guardrails, which are capture-pass assignments.
- The narration is truthful: the coordination_note is set only when the refused objective differs from the centre, and the DIM-RETURNS note loop skips the unit.
- The report is candid: bench_fires 0, the broader first version that was narrowed, and the risks.
- It rebases onto 1.56.8 with one trivial conflict (both add constants after FIX_LONE_FLIP). It has no logic interaction with WAAAGH-ADV-CHARGE (on) or R1-SUPPORT-ADVANCE / R1-HOME-LAST (off).
- It cannot make any bench game worse.
reviews.summary:
Verdict: ok as code. The design is narrow and correct, but it never fires in the benchmark, which decides shipping.

- **Bench:** it fires 0 times per game in all three fixtures, because no bench list has a Heavy weapon. It cannot help or hurt the bench, and the V2-1 gate will PARK it, so picking it ships nothing for this cluster.
- **Where it fires** (Lootas armies, at most one unit per player per game, round 1): the evidence splits by matchup. The three Orks-mirror findings measured +5.6, +4.8 and +2.6. Every measured Orks-vs-Custodes 'Lootas to the centre' position is harmful or neutral. Its one observed fire in that matchup (s7490, Lootas Gamma) repeats the harmful guardrail's move with the twin unit, and has not been measured.
- **Other risks outside the evidence:** it also overrides deep-strike denial screens; the Heavy gate admits Space Marine Intercessors and Infiltrators and Space Wolves Scouts; the 'refused its pick' precondition in practice means any leftover; and rounds 3+ are unmeasured (the H2 re-check is pending).

None of these is a demonstrated loss on the bench, so I found no major issue. If it is ever un-parked, first:
1. Move it below the denial-screen branch.
2. Restrict it to fragile units whose Heavy weapons are not Assault.
3. Value-check its own fires at s7490 r1 P1, s7462 r1 P1 and s7466 r1 P2 at horizon 2, and require all three findings to confirm at H2.

issues.situation: The fix copies the centre candidate's own action (`assignments[unit_id] = rc_cand.duplicate()`). An `advance` order runs in the ADVANCE branch (base line 7089), which comes before any hold check. A `move` order goes through the NORMAL MOVE branch (line 7191), where the MOV-1 hold and then the T7-26 Heavy hold (line 7303, `_should_hold_for_heavy_bonus`) run. T7-26 releases the unit only when centroid-to-marker distance <= M, or when score >= 10 and distance <= 2M. A 2-turn walking candidate sits at gap + 3.79", so for M6 at gap 8.2-12" T7-26 still holds the unit whenever an enemy is in Heavy range (that enemy is also why the RACE-1 long Advance was refused). In that case the fix logs "[RANGED_CENTRE] ... joining X at the centre", uses its one-per-plan slot, adds 1 to support_counts[centre] (so later leftovers' support fallback avoids the centre), and cancels the unit's corridor block or screen. The unit then "holds for Heavy weapon bonus (obj obj_center)": the failure this fix targets, plus a lost block. Lootas avoid this only at gaps of 6-11" and 12-19" (Advance candidates); they still hit it at 11-12", and at <=6" when the score is < 10. Non-Lootas Heavy units (SW Scout Squads with missile launchers, SM Intercessors with bolt rifles) hit it at any 2-turn walking distance. The test's own Lootas is a 1-turn `move` 8" from the marker at M6, which T7-26 re-holds unless its score is >= 10. The test never checks this. The tag is also printed at plan time, so it would count toward the V2-1 fix gate even when no decision changed.
issues.proposed_change: Accept the centre candidate only if `rc_c.action == "advance"`, which is what all three findings measured. Alternatively, accept a `move` candidate only when the executor would not re-hold it: skip when `_should_hold_for_heavy_bonus(unit, centroid, rc_pos, enemies, M, rc_c, _get_unit_heavy_weapon_data(unit))` or `_should_hold_for_shooting(unit, centroid, rc_pos, _get_max_weapon_range(unit), enemies, M, rc_c)` is true, and log the skip. Move the test squad into an Advance geometry (for example centroid ~11" from the centre: gap 7.2" gives a round-1 Advance to a no-man's-land objective). Add one execution-level assertion that the unit's movement decision is BEGIN_ADVANCE toward obj_center, not REMAIN_STATIONARY.

issues.situation: The fix depends on a false positive in the base AI's ability-text check. At the findings (Lootas gaps 14.9-16.8" to the centre, enemies 27-45" away, inside the 48" Deffgun range), the 2-turn centre candidate exists only because `_should_unit_advance_long_trip` (line 12098) finds "advance" in Waaagh! and "shoot" in Dat's Our Loot! Walking, those trips take 3 turns and fail the fix's `turns_to_reach <= 2` gate. 1.56.8 kept this text check in RACE-1. issues.situation: The LONE-TRIP override is all-or-nothing. One friend moving to the centre lifts LONE-TRIP for a fragile squad (Lootas are T5, 1 wound per model) whatever the friend's OC or arrival turn, for example a 1-OC Mek or a 3-turn trip against 48 enemy OC. That is the round-3 failure LONE-TRIP was added to stop. The base check `lone_trip` (line 10312) skips when threat > army and threat >= 2.0 x ours, where ours counts only friends arriving no later.
issues.proposed_change: Before overriding, re-run the LONE-TRIP OC test with the friends going to the centre counted whatever their arrival turn (and incoming OC). Skip when lone_trip_oc.threat >= MOVE_RACE_HOPELESS_RATIO x (ours + friends' alive OC). At s7462 the fix still fires (threat ~30 < 2.0 x (10 + 10)); at s7463 the friends are two Battlewagons.

Move the block after the denial-screen branch (it stays before screen-protect and corridor block, so all findings are kept), or say in the comment that denial screens are overridden too. reviews.strengths: It is the smallest possible change: about 45 lines in one place (the top of the pass-3 leftover loop), with no scoring change and no new state outside the function. FIX_RANGED_CENTRE = 0 is the first operand of the gate, so the whole block is skipped and the base is restored exactly; the only difference is one extra param-read telemetry entry. The gates are tight: round 1, a refused pick, Heavy, ranged, not a melee seeker, a centre candidate within 2 turns, a friend going there, and one per plan. Because of them, keepers, capture-pass units and later rounds are untouched by construction, which covers guardrails s7490 (keeper), s7466 (capture Advance), s7470 (race), s7462 r3 and the new r5c06 s7481 round-1 Lootas captures. At all three findings the code reproduces the measured alternative exactly: the Lootas are 14.9-16.8" from the centre, which gives a RACE-1 2-turn Advance candidate, and Advance executes before T7-26. The [RANGED_CENTRE] log line is informative (action, turns, score, friends, refused pick), the coordination_note is accurate, support_counts stays consistent, and no debug log was removed. The test pins and erases the override, fails on base for the right reason (the two join asserts), covers round 2, melee, non-Heavy, no-friend and param-0 cases, and drives the real planner rather than a helper. reviews.summary: This is a clean, correctly gated narrow patch at /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/.ai_lab_work/wt_panel_rh/tools/ai_lab/r5_designs/ranged_hold_vs_centre/narrow.patch. A value of 0 restores the base exactly. It reproduces the measured Advance-to-centre at s7462, s7463 and s7460, and by construction leaves every listed guardrail decision alone, including the new r5c06 Lootas captures. It has one real but latent bug: it copies the candidate's own action, and a `move` centre order still passes through MOV-1 and T7-26 when it executes (base lines 7191-7316). For 2-turn walks (gap 8.2-12" at M6) T7-26 still holds a Heavy unit, so the fix logs a centre push, uses its slot, adds to support_counts and cancels a block, while the unit holds anyway. Fix it by requiring `advance`, or by pre-checking `_should_hold_for_heavy_bonus` and `_should_hold_for_shooting` on the candidate, and add an execution-level test assert. For shipping, the decisive fact is that no unit in any of the three bench fixtures has a Heavy weapon. It therefore fires 0 times per game by construction, fails the V2-1 fix gate and should be parked with FIX_RANGED_CENTRE = 0. Two further risks: at the findings its 2-turn reach exists only because RACE-1 misreads Lootas' Waaagh! + Dat's Our Loot! text as Advance-and-Shoot (a V2-4 fix of that heuristic would silently switch the design off), and its LONE-TRIP override needs only one friend of any OC. Other points are minor: gate details, test gaps, and report evidence notes (s7460 base label, unmeasured knock-on fires at s7490 and s7466).

issues.situation: Round 1 of every bench game, from the fixed postdeploy start, so the candidate's P1 plan is essentially the same in every game where it is P1. The fix measures reach as the gap from the single nearest model to the hosting area. A multi-model unit whose nearest model is within M, but whose centroid gap (base: centroid to marker minus 3.79") is above M, changes from an Advance to a Normal move priced at 1 turn. The planner still books the unit's full OC (apply_capture_assignment's obj_oc_remaining, LONE-TRIP 'ours', race_our_oc). The executor still walks the centroid toward the marker, so only the front model(s) reach the area, sometimes none. I translated each model straight toward the marker on the real fixture saves (40k/tests/saves/*_2000_postdeploy.w40ksave): (a) Custodes mirror and asym, Custodian Guard Gamma to the centre: base gap 11.0" (long-trip Advance; a roll of 3+ puts 5/5 models on the ruin) becomes a Normal move (nearest model 5.09"). After 6" only 1 of 5 models is on the area (OC 2 vs the OC 10 booked). The candidate also loses the 2-turn contest race (x0.5), the distance penalty and the round-1 -2, and gains +3 reachability, so it very likely wins. (b) Orks mirror, Deffkoptas Beta to the centre: priced as a 1-turn Normal move (nearest model 11.47" at M12), but a 12" move toward the marker leaves that model 0.91" short (0/6 on the area). (c) Normal move vs Advance (models on the area): Stormboyz Alpha to the centre 3/5 vs 5/5; Stormboyz Delta to NML 2/5 vs 5/5; Warbikers Gamma to NML 4/6 vs 6/6; Deffkoptas Alpha to the centre 3/6 vs 6/6 (roll 2+). Many of these flips are never logged: when the base long-trip Advance was already priced at 1 turn, turns do not drop, so no [RANGED_CENTRE] line is written. Example: Stormboyz Alpha, 14.7" at M12, ceil(14.7/15.5)=1. The reported 19 lines per game therefore undercount the changed decisions. Measured positions agree. In the 9 measured round-1 cases comparing the AI's Advance with a Normal move to the same objective, the Normal move was never clearly better and 5 were harmful. The fix flips 5 of those 9 to the Normal move: s7407 Scouts -5.00 (harmful), s7417 Lootas -6.67 (harmful), s7481 r1 P2 Lootas Alpha to obj_nml_1 -18.50 (corrected gap 5.52" <= M6; this breaks the explicit new guardrail), s7423 -3.83, s7416 Custodian Guard -2.00. The last has no Heavy weapon, so its measured branch is the fix's own Normal-move path. Caveat: for the Heavy-armed Lootas and Scouts, the base's measured 'Normal move' branch probably fell into the T7-26 Heavy hold. The fix's real Normal move (front 1-3 models on the edge) is unmeasured there.
issues.proposed_change: Do not ship this as the cluster fix. If an 11e reach correction is kept at all: (1) It must never change the mode. When the base gap would Advance (advance window or RACE-1 long_adv), keep action = 'advance' and only lower turns_to_reach. (2) Price arrival from the models that carry the OC, not from the single nearest model. For example, use the host gap of the k-th nearest alive model, where the k nearest models' OC >= min(unit_oc, the objective's remaining need). (3) When a trip is priced by the area, aim _compute_movement_toward_target at the nearest point of the hosting area, not at the marker, so execution matches the price.

issues.situation: The trigger is the whole planner on the bench, one-sided, and unrelated to the cluster's evidence. All 5 objectives in all 3 bench fixtures (layout take_and_hold_mirror_1) are terrain-hosted, so every capture candidate in every movement phase, in every round, is repriced. At the start positions the corrected gap is 3.7-4.7" shorter on average (max 7.8"). 46-61% of (unit, objective) prices lose a Normal-move turn: 74/162 Orks mirror, 66/108 Custodes mirror, 69/134 asym. Only our own reach changes. enemy_arrivals and projected_enemy_oc (and friendly_arrivals) are still computed centroid to marker minus 3.79", at M+2" per move. The centre ruin on the bench extends 5-7.2" from its marker, so enemy units whose front model is one move from the area are not counted. That makes LONE-TRIP's 1-move window and the contest race systematically favour our trips: the round-2 FAR_TRIP/OVERCOMMIT lesson in reverse, for fragile Stormboyz, Gretchin and lone Wartrikes. The bench armies have no Lootas and no Heavy weapons (0 Heavy holds in the 6 reach games; every unit lists heavy=[]). The bench therefore tests a general reach repricing that no measured position covers, not the ranged-hold fix. Its only full-game pair (Orks mirror) was -7.5 VP. reviews.summary:
Verdict: drop it as the fix for this cluster. It is a board-wide reach repricing, not a ranged-hold fix. On the bench every objective is a terrain area, so it changes every movement phase in every fixture, yet the bench has no Lootas and no Heavy weapons. The bench would test a general change that no measured position covers.

Its core metric is the gap from our single nearest model to the area. That is the first-touch reach, while every downstream term books the unit's full OC. It is applied to our units only; enemy arrivals stay centroid-to-marker. It also silently turns Advances into Normal moves. On the real fixture saves:
- Custodian Guard Gamma to the centre (Custodes mirror and asym) becomes a 1-turn Normal move that puts 1 of 5 models on the ruin. A 3+ Advance roll puts 5 of 5.
- Deffkoptas Beta to the centre is priced as a 1-turn arrival and ends with 0 of 6 models on the area.
- Stormboyz and Warbikers arrive with 2-4 of their models instead of all of them.

In the measured positions, the same Advance-to-Normal flip hits 5 of the 9 round-1 Advance-vs-Normal cases, including the explicit s7481 guardrail. None of the 9 favoured the Normal move. The Heavy-hold caveat applies to 4 of those 5.

It reproduces none of the three findings' measured alternatives, and its only full-game pair was -7.5 VP.

A sound version would be a separate, symmetric, OC-weighted 11e reach model that never changes the move mode. That belongs on the rules-audit track with its own bench.

All 5 objectives on these layouts are terrain-hosted, so every trip is affected.

(1) New r5c06 guardrail, s7481 r1 P2, Lootas Alpha -> obj_nml_1. Centroid gap 9.2"; base = long-trip Advance at 1 turn (the Waaagh!/Dat's Our Loot! text heuristic makes Lootas count as advance-and-shoot, P=0.5). Nearest model is 5.52" (<= M6), so the patch makes it a 1-turn Normal MOVE; the centre (4.84") is also a Normal move. Turns stay 1, so no [RANGED_CENTRE] line fires. A rigid translation along centroid->marker lands 3/8 models after a Normal move vs 8/8 after the Advance; the NORMAL MOVE branch can also blend Lootas (Rapid Fire, enemy 30" away) 40% toward half range. (3) s7481 r1 P1 Gamma -> obj_nml_2 keeps its Advance only because the gap is 6.017" vs M6. At 6.0" a Normal move lands 0/10.

1. Measure the area reach in a way that matches the OC the plan books. Use the k-th nearest alive model's area gap, with k = models needed to cover the OC booked there (oc_consumed / per-model OC), or at least the median model or centroid->area distance. Use that measure for turns_to_reach, the reachability bonus and the move/advance choice.
2. Keep 'advance' whenever an Advance lands more of the booked OC than a Normal move.
3. Add guardrail tests at s7481 r1 P2 (BEGIN_ADVANCE toward obj_nml_1), s7481 r1 P1 (BEGIN_ADVANCE toward obj_nml_2) and s7466 r1 P2.

Geometry with the median-model measure:
- s7481 P2 = 7.0", s7481 P1 = 8.0", s7466 = 8.0": all stay Advance-now (guardrails kept).
- F1 Alpha = 11.2": still 2 turns.

issues.situation: Asymmetric race. Only our candidate unit is measured from its nearest model to the hosting area. _evaluate_all_objectives (untouched) still builds projected_enemy_oc, enemy_arrivals and friendly_arrivals from centroid->marker minus 3.79" at M+2" per move. With the trip priced at 1 turn, LONE-TRIP's threat becomes enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc. Example: an enemy Lootas unit at F1's mirror position (centroid 19.6" from the marker, nearest model 7.8" from the area) reaches the area in one Advance by the patch's own measure, yet adds 0 to projected_enemy_oc (19.6" > 11.79"). Contests on every terrain objective therefore look easier for us than for them. That pushes fragile units forward, which is the round-3 REINFORCE-CAP failure mode (enemy reach undercounted). The report lists this as its risk (2) but does not fix it.
issues.proposed_change: When FIX_RANGED_CENTRE is on, compute projected_enemy_oc, enemy_arrivals.moves and friendly_arrivals.moves with the same per-unit hosting-area gap as our candidate (same k-th-model measure as above). _ri_enemy_next_move_oc already does nearest-model -> hosting-area for RI-RACE and can be reused. Cache the result per (unit, objective) once per plan.

issues.situation: The [RANGED_CENTRE] line is a pricing line, not a decision line. It fires whenever an assigned trip's turns dropped, even if the unit would have made the same move. It stays silent on equal-turn action flips (s7481 r1 P2: 1-turn Advance -> 1-turn Normal move; corrected gaps in (M+5, M+6] where an Advance becomes a 2-turn walk) and on re-assignments (F3's drop to a corridor block). The designer's 19/game is therefore not the decision-change rate the protocol-v2 bench-reach gate needs. Separately, the Heavy-skip line can describe a counterfactual: at s7481 P2 the base would have Advanced and never reached T7-26.
issues.proposed_change: Shadow-compute the base action from the uncorrected gap next to rc_turns_base. Emit a decision-level [RANGED_CENTRE] line only when the assigned unit's (objective, action) differs from the base-priced choice. Keep the reprice line as debug-only.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Fires constantly, in all three fixtures. They all use the take_and_hold_mirror_1 layout, and all 5 objectives there are terrain-hosted (area-large-1/2/13/14 and centre trapezoids 43+44). Part (a) therefore re-measures every candidate in every movement plan of the fix's seat (the plan is cached, so about 10 plans per game).

Geometry-only estimate for round 1 from the postdeploy saves:
- About 45% of candidates change turn count (25/54 per Custodes seat, 35/81 per Orks seat).
- About 19-21 Orks candidates per seat flip from Advance to Normal move, because the base text heuristic makes most Ork units advance-and-shoot. Custodes flip about 4.

- Heavy-hold skips: 0, since Heavy holds never occur on the bench per the reach run. The T7-26 part is inert there; all the effect comes from planner repricing.

Real decision changes are very likely several per game with Orks (mirror and asym) and at least 1 per game in the Custodes mirror. The raw [RANGED_CENTRE] count would pass the v2 reach gate, but it is not decision-level: it counts unchanged decisions and misses equal-turn Advance->Normal flips.
reviews.strengths:
- **Param 0 restores base exactly.** The rc block, the candidate keys and the log loop are all gated on rc_on. The action branch reuses rc_adv_now through a lazy ternary, so _should_unit_advance runs once and prints once. In T7-26 the new checks are dominated by the base checks when gap_in is absent or the flag is off.
- **Null-safe.** hd_mm null means no host areas; _rc_host_gap_inches returns INF with no method or no models, and minf absorbs it. Dead models are skipped. Only movable units are scored, and no other code reads the new keys.
- **Cheap.** _assign_units_to_objectives runs once per movement phase per player (_turn_movement_plan cache), so the per-model area scan is negligible.
- **Logging rules respected.** New lines go to both print and the debug log, and no debug log was removed.
- **The diagnosis is partly right.** Centroid->marker does overstate reach to large 11e areas: F1 Alpha 15.8\" vs median model 11.2\". Part (b) fixes a real base inconsistency: an (M, M+2] Advance-now trip was priced at 2 turns while a longer long-trip Advance was priced at 1.
- **The report is candid and checks out.** It admits F1 matches only at army level, F2 is unchanged, F3 changes the wrong way, and the one bench pair was -7.5. Its decision and guardrail claims match my geometry: Gamma 5.24\", s7466 6.7\" keeps the Advance, s7470 centre unchanged.
- **One sound test.** The fabricated test pins part (b) through the real planner and fails on base for the right reason.
reviews.summary:
FIX_RANGED_CENTRE re-prices every trip to an 11e terrain objective. It measures reach from the nearest alive model to the hosting area, and prices a trip the plan Advances on now (gap in (M, M+2]) at 1 turn. The code is cleanly gated (param 0 = base exactly), null-safe and cheap.

The core proxy is a real bug. The first model touching the area sets the turns and the move-vs-Advance choice, while the plan books the unit's full OC. The worst case is the new r5c06 guardrail, s7481 r1 P2. There it turns the measured-right round-1 Lootas Advance onto obj_nml_1 into a Normal move (nearest model 5.52\" <= M6, centroid gap 9.2\"). The Normal move lands about 3/8 models instead of 8/8. The flip is silent, because the turn count stays 1 and no [RANGED_CENTRE] line fires. At F1 the centre goes to Gamma by a Normal move that lands 1-2/10 models while the plan books 10 OC there. The race is also asymmetric: enemy and friendly arrivals still use centroid->marker.

The design fires broadly on the bench, because all bench objectives are terrain-hosted. Its one bench pair was -7.5, F2 is unchanged and F3 moved the wrong way. With an OC-consistent area measure (k-th or median model), symmetric arrivals and a keep-Advance rule, my geometry says the guardrails hold (s7481 P1/P2, s7466). But F1 then reduces to Gamma Advancing to the centre (army level), and F2/F3 stay unchanged. The revised design therefore needs new measurement and is expected to help this cluster only a little.

Saves decoded to JSON for these geometry checks are under /tmp/rh_review/saves/; scripts are /tmp/rh_review/geom.py, sim_move.py and bench_breadth.py. Nothing was replayed in Godot.

issues.situation: Wrong distance on 11th-edition terrain objectives. This affects every fire on every bench and sweep board. On the bench, obj_center is hosted by area-trapezoid-43/44, an 11.5" x 10" box. The engine counts a model in range only when its base overlaps a hosting area (MissionManager.model_in_objective_range and model_gap_to_objective_range_px). _ranged_centre_redirect instead measures gap = model-centre distance to the marker point - 3.79". Computed from the saves, this overstates the gap by 1.1-7.3" (design gap / true gap): s7462 r1 P2 Lootas Gamma 12.5/5.2 and Alpha 12.9/7.8; s7460 P1 Alpha 12.6/6.2; s7466 P2 Gamma 9.7/6.7; bench Prosecutors 12.2/8.1; bench Warbikers B 21.7/17.4. The Normal-vs-Advance rule (Advance only if gap > 2M) uses this wrong number and gives the wrong move type in 3 of 10 sampled geometries. (a) At s7462, the unit the design actually redirects (Gamma) Advances and loses its whole round-1 Deffgun volley, although a 6" Normal move already puts it on the centre area (infantry cross ruins with no penalty). (b) A Lootas in the s7466 geometry (true gap 6.7") gets a Normal move that stops 0.7" short. It misses the round-1 arrival and the round-2 Command-phase score, which is the value the design claims. The measured analogues for Normal-instead-of-Advance in round 1 are harmful: -6.67 [-10.64,-2.69] at s7466 and -9.33 / -18.50 for the r5c06 Lootas captures. (c) Bench Warbikers B have only Assault guns, so Advancing costs them no shooting and reaches the area 1 time in 3, but they get a Normal move. The reach gate and the closest-unit pick use the same wrong gap.
issues.proposed_change: Compute the gap per model with the engine predicate the AI already uses for FIX-HELD-DUP. Set od = _held_dup_objective_at(snapshot, c_pos) and mm = _held_dup_mm(). When both exist, gap = mm.model_gap_to_objective_range_px(model, od) / PIXELS_PER_INCH; otherwise keep the marker formula. Use this gap for the reach gate, the closest-unit pick and the mode. Choose a Normal move only if gap <= M: the unit arrives this turn and keeps its volley. Otherwise Advance: it arrives this turn if gap <= M+6, else it gets as close as possible for round 2. Also Advance when every ranged weapon is Assault. Then replay the 3 findings and 6 guardrails; at s7462, Gamma should now make a Normal move onto the area.

issues.situation: The design almost never runs on the bench. The Heavy branch cannot fire: no ranged weapon in mirror_custodes, mirror_orks or asym_2000_postdeploy has 'heavy'. The corridor-block branch can only reach screening candidates that have guns and are not melee seekers: Prosecutors (Custodes) and the two 3-model Warbikers units A/B (Orks). One of them would need a round-1 corridor block guarding a marker other than the centre while the centre is not enemy-held. The designer's Orks pair had no round-1 blocks, and P2's centre was already enemy-held. The Custodes fixtures show only ~2 'approaching' GEL lines per game across all 5 rounds, and Custodes Prosecutors in the round-1 sweeps capture, hold or screen; they never block. Expected ~0 fires per game. That fails the V2-1 fix gate (>= 1.0 per game) and would give identical bench pairs (like V9's 64/64).

issues.situation: The only enemy check is whether the enemy controls the centre now. At s7462 the redirect sends a fragile W1 unit to the centre that the shipped LONE-TRIP (1.56.6) had just vetoed ('not going alone to obj_center'). That override was right there (+5.63 n24). issues.situation: The scope is wider than the evidence. Corridor blocks that guard the player's own HOME marker are eligible, and so are Heavy-hold 'move' entries aimed at home. issues.situation: Later-round costs are not measured. The redirected unit (10 models, 1 wound each) stands in the open centre. reviews.fires_in_bench: About 0 per game; upper bound about 0.3 per game in the Custodes fixtures. The designer measured 0 in one Orks-mirror pair. Why: (1) The Heavy branch cannot fire. No ranged weapon in any of the 3 bench lists has the 'heavy' rule (I checked every unit in the decoded mirror_custodes, mirror_orks and asym_2000_postdeploy saves). (2) The corridor-block branch needs a screening candidate (not a CHARACTER; <=100 pts with OC<=2, or <=150 pts with no guns) that also has ranged weapons and is not a melee seeker. That leaves only Prosecutors (1 per Custodes army) and Warbikers A/B (3-model, 60-pt units) per Ork army. Bench Gretchin count as melee seekers (Runtherd tools S5), as do Stormboyz (Choppa AP-1). One of these units would need a round-1 corridor block guarding a marker other than the centre, while the centre is not enemy-held. The Orks mirror had no round-1 blocks, and P2's centre is held after P1's round 1: Wazdakka starts 14.9" from the centre point and the hosting area is 11.5" x 10". reviews.strengths: It is narrow and respects the guardrails by construction (checked in the code). It runs in battle round 1 only and moves one unit per player. It never touches: 'hold' keepers (s7490); 'advance' races and captures (s7470, s7466, and the r5c06 Lootas Advance captures s7481); screens protecting friendly units; plan-earmarked units; blocks guarding the centre (s7435, s7462 P1); an enemy-held centre. Later rounds are unchanged (s7462 r3), so it cannot hold units back in rounds 2-5, which was the FAR_TRIP/OVERCOMMIT failure. Its forward bias matches the secondary-card lesson. FIX_RANGED_CENTRE=0 skips the pass, and the new protects_objective field and quiet flag do nothing in that case. It uses no RNG, so bench games where it does not fire stay identical (the designer saw 589 identical actions). It changes the decision at all three findings: exactly at s7463 and s7460, and at s7462 through the sibling Lootas. It logs its own [RANGED_CENTRE] tag (a print plus a thinking step) for the V2-1 gate. The claim cache is cleared in reset_caches, which runs per game for each seat.

Through the game-impact lens, this design cannot make the AI worse on the bench, because it essentially never fires there. None of the 3 bench lists has a Heavy weapon, and the corridor-block branch can only reach Prosecutors and two 3-model Warbikers units, which rarely block in round 1. Expected fires are about 0 per game: it fails the V2-1 fix gate (park) and bench pairs would be identical. In games where it does fire (lists with Lootas), there is one major flaw. Its gap, reach gate and Normal/Advance choice measure to the marker point minus 3.79". But every bench and sweep board uses 11th-edition terrain-hosted centres, where a model is in range when its base is on the hosting area. The true gap is 1.1-7.3" smaller, so the move type is wrong in 3 of 10 sampled geometries. At s7462 the redirected Gamma Advances and loses its volley although a Normal move already arrives. At the s7466 geometry it would make the Normal move that the measured analogue says loses 6.67 VP. It also ignores Assault weapons. Fix: use the engine's model_gap_to_objective_range_px, and choose a Normal move only when gap <= M. Smaller fixes: add a one-move threat guard (it keeps all 3 findings); exclude blocks guarding home and Heavy-hold moves aimed at home; require CONFIRMED-H2 for s7462 and s7463. Verdict: revise. issues.situation: Mode rule `mode = "advance" if best_gap > 2*M else "move"`: an idle M6 Lootas 6-12" from the centre's control range gets BEGIN_NORMAL_MOVE. In exactly this band, round-1 measurements found a Normal move to the centre worse than the AI's Advance: s7417 r1 P2 Lootas Beta (gap 11.7") -6.67 harmful, s7466 r1 P2 Lootas Gamma (gap 9.7") -6.67 harmful (a cluster guardrail), s7407 r1 P2 Scout Squad (gap 8.3") -5.00 harmful. On the bench, Warbikers B (gap 18.6-21.7", at most 24") would get a Normal move although its twin dakkaguns are Assault, so an Advance costs it no shooting.

issues.situation: Snapshot contract: the new mutable static `_ranged_centre_claims` is not in `_snapshot_planning_state()` / `_restore_planning_state()`. `suggest_action` (the K hint, through `AIPlayer.request_suggestion`) is documented as truly side-effect-free. Scenario: in round-1 movement a human presses K; the preview's plan claims idle unit X; the restore leaves the claim behind. The human then moves X elsewhere, and every later K that round hits `not assignments.has(claimed_uid)` and returns early, so the next idle unit is never suggested for the centre. `_suggest_in_progress_move` previews with a single unit's actions and can claim that unit the same way. The bench and live AI turns are not affected, because AIPlayer refuses previews during `_processing_turn` and `reset_caches` runs on load or reset.
issues.proposed_change: Add `"ranged_centre_claims": _ranged_centre_claims.duplicate(true)` to `_snapshot_planning_state()` and `_ranged_centre_claims = s["ranged_centre_claims"]` to `_restore_planning_state()`. Add a contract test like `test_ai_plan_earmarks.test_snapshot_contract`.

issues.situation: There is no threat or OC check at the centre. The only guard is 'state not enemy_weak/enemy_strong now', which misses enemy units that can Advance onto the marker (the round-3 REINFORCE-CAP lesson). So the pass can override a LONE-TRIP, RACE-ARMY or DIM-RETURNS refusal of the centre: a fragile unit (Lootas W1, Prosecutors T3 W1) kept off the centre because 'the enemy can have ~X OC there' then Heavy-holds or blocks, and gets sent there alone. It also ignores friendly OC already heading to the centre. At s7462 Beta already advances there and Gamma is added. It can also pull a Heavy-holding unit off a trip to our own home marker. These cases are unmeasured: the s7462 finding supports overriding there, but LONE-TRIP was itself value-checked.
issues.proposed_change: Skip the redirect when the centre's projected threat (`enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc`, or the race OC) is at least 2x the OC the plan has there including this unit, unless another friendly unit is already assigned to the centre. Also skip when the old entry's objective is our home marker.

issues.situation: Bench reach is about 0, so the V2-1 fix gate (at least 1.0 per game) will park this design. No unit in any of the 3 bench lists has a Heavy ranged weapon (checked in the decoded saves), so the Heavy branch is dead there. Only Prosecutors A (Custodes) and Warbikers A/B (Orks) pass the corridor branch's static gates, and they start 2.6" and 0.3-9.7" from their home markers' range. issues.proposed_change: Either accept parking, with the code kept and the param set to 0, or widen the idle definition so it can reach the bench. Options: include the MOV-1 and threat holds, and round-1 support moves that end 2 or more moves from any marker. Re-measure guardrails after widening.

issues.situation: The plan-time `[RANGED_CENTRE]` print and thinking step run on every re-plan. When a unit becomes movable after the plan or moves again, the claimed unit is redirected and logged again. A V2-1 count of the fix's log tag can then exceed the decisions that actually changed; only consecutive duplicate lines are collapsed.
issues.proposed_change: Count the decision-level line instead (the unit's move description carries "RANGED-CENTRE:" once, when it acts), or print the plan-time line only when the claim is first set.

issues.situation: Probe fidelity, latent. Base execution sets `has_ranged_weapons = false` for a transport VEHICLE with melee weapons, and for loaded transports, before T7-26, so such a unit never Heavy-holds. reviews.strengths: The gating is exact: the call is gated on FIX_RANGED_CENTRE >= 0.5, `rc_going` is true only for entries the pass wrote, and the `protects_objective` key and the `quiet=false` default are inert, so param 0 gives base behaviour. The trigger is narrow: battle round 1 only, and only idle plan entries (a Heavy hold probed through the real `_should_hold_for_heavy_bonus`, or a T7-42 block guarding a non-centre marker). Keepers (hold), units already advancing (so the s7481 Lootas advance-captures are untouched), other screens, earmarked units, melee seekers, loaded transports, centre-guarding blocks and an enemy-held centre are all left alone. All 6 cluster guardrails hold by construction, and the change cannot repeat the round-2 later-round hold-back failure. It is a plan-level (COORD-4) rewrite, so the announced plan is what executes, and the unit's move text carries "RANGED-CENTRE:" as a decision-level line. A one-per-player cap, persisted across re-plans, bounds overcommit. Cost is negligible: once per plan build in round 1, units x models. I recomputed the report's decision checks from the saves and they match the code: s7463 Alpha (gap 13.2") and s7460 Alpha (12.6") get exactly the measured Advance to obj_center; at s7462 the sibling Gamma (12.5") is picked over Alpha (12.9"), as the report says. reviews.summary: Review of /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/.ai_lab_work/wt_panel_rh/tools/ai_lab/r5_designs/ranged_hold_vs_centre/game.patch and game.json against 12e0753. The code is correct and tightly gated: at param 0 the AI behaves exactly as base, and I found no bug that changes AI-vs-AI play. I applied the patch to a scratch copy, traced every changed path, and recomputed unit gaps from the case saves; the report's decision and guardrail checks agree with the code. No issue is major, but these should be fixed before any merge. (1) `_ranged_centre_claims` is missing from the suggest_action snapshot contract, so a K preview in round 1 leaks a claim that suppresses later hints that round. (2) The redirected entry keeps a stale coordination_note, so the game log says "staying with the army" right before the unit advances to the centre. (3) The Normal-move mode for gap <= 2M is unmeasured, and three round-1 measurements in that exact band found a Normal move worse than an Advance (-5.0 to -6.7); use "move" only when it reaches range this turn. (4) The test misses the corridor-block branch, which is the only one that can reach the bench and covers the s7463 finding, and it never exercises the hold-check bypass. Design risks: there is no threat or OC check at the centre, so the pass can undo LONE-TRIP refusals for fragile units, and it ignores units already heading there. The deciding practical point is bench reach of about 0: the Heavy branch is dead on all three fixtures, and the corridor branch only fits Prosecutors and Warbikers A/B, which start next to their home markers. The design should therefore be expected to be PARKED by the V2-1 fix gate (at least 1.0 per game) unless its idle definition is widened. It is a reasonable, safe fix for Lootas-heavy lists, but it cannot show a gain on the current benchmark.
